basis: BACH2-related immunodeficiency with intrinsic immune enterocolitis in 2/3 and bronchiectasis in 2/3; reactive blood-count changes alone do not establish hematologic disease.
Defined by impaired cardiac function; activity limitation does not establish damage to other organs.
Nonsyndromic bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in 4/4 patients; vestibular dysfunction also belongs to the otologic axis.
Cerebral arterial disease causing infarction and permanent injury of brain tissue in the middle cerebral artery territory.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; structural scoliosis reported in 1/3 (~33%). Widely spaced teeth alone do not establish dental functional damage.
Bilateral congenital fusion of the humerus and radius directly affects bones and elbow mobility.
Benign vascular neoplasm; anatomical sites vary across this umbrella, so no additional site applies consistently.
Genetic susceptibility subtype of immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the disease.
Testicular germ-cell tumor of reproductive origin; neither endocrine dysfunction nor another covered organ is intrinsic to this histologic subtype.
Defined by malformed enlarged teeth and sensorineural hearing loss, both usually present. Ocular malformations occur in only 5–29%.
Inherited marrow disorder with erythroid and granulocytic hypoplasia, anemia and neutropenia in 2/2 patients.
Structural narrowing of the lacrimal drainage apparatus, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Defined by callosal agenesis, infantile spasms and chorioretinal lacunae; vertebral/rib malformations and scoliosis are frequent (30–79%).
Endotoxin-triggered immune-mediated small-vessel injury with intravascular coagulation and thrombosis; skin and renal necrosis vary by localized or generalized form.
Direct disease of extraocular skeletal muscles, affecting the ocular adnexa and muscle function; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
KMT2B-related neurodevelopmental dystonia; astigmatism affects 3/6 (~50%), supporting ocular functional involvement. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Papillary epithelial neoplasm originating in intrahepatic bile ducts; bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Infantile interstitial lung disease with pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia; no systemic endocrine disorder is defined.
Drug-induced loss of bone mass and strength defines this disease; an intrinsic endocrine disorder is not required.
Congenital infection with defining CNS and ocular injury; hepatic disease with jaundice/hepatosplenomegaly is a major syndrome feature. Hearing injury varies and is omitted by cap.
Cranioskeletal and nail dysplasia; tubulointerstitial disease/CKD in 2/2 and retinal dystrophy/visual loss in 1/1 assessed. Dental and developmental findings omitted by cap.
SETBP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder; visual impairment occurs in 14/29 (~48%), hypermetropia in 9/29 (~31%) and ptosis in 3/4.
Portal vascular liver disease; splenomegaly in 9/9 and hypersplenic thrombocytopenia in 8/9 (~89%). Esophageal varices are vascular involvement.
Invasive hepatic Echinococcus infection; extrahepatic lesions occur in <30%. Reactive eosinophilia and inflammatory anemia do not establish direct hematologic injury.
Inherited skin disorder with absent dermatoglyphics, blistering and milia; persistent digital flexion contractures occur in 8/8 assessed patients.
